headline: Curated peptide databases and ADMET models for therapeutic property prediction
label: Peptide Databases And Prediction Tools
summary: Peptide therapeutics are expanding, and permeability, stability, and inconsistent evaluation practices now constrain how predictive models are compared.
synthesis: The dominant thread is curation of peptide-specific data paired with predictive models of pharmacological properties. DBNAMP provides 1,859 antimicrobial peptide entries with noncanonical residues, modifications, and 3D conformers, and ADMETatlas compiles peptide ADMET evidence centered on permeability and in vivo stability. Pepti-DrugPhAI processes SMILES and amino acid sequences jointly to predict peptide ADMET properties and toxicity. A review of antibacterial peptide databases and ML/DL prediction tools identifies leakage and inconsistent evaluation and proposes a reference evaluation framework. M2iOR, an atlas of insect odorant receptor-odorant interactions, lies outside the peptide setting but shares the emphasis on quantitative, context-resolved interaction data. What is new here is the pairing of chemically explicit representations with standardized evaluation, which constrains how claims of predictive performance can be compared across these resources.
